anchors.statement: The installer must accept --github and --azure flags that select the provider commands rendered into the sc-compose templates.
anchors.quote: could we add --github and --azure flags which inject the proper commands into sc-compose j2 templates?
anchors.scope: adds or changes the installer, provider vars files, sc_render or templates that run PR commands
anchors.deterministic_check: atm-bd skill --azure renders a dispatch template containing 'az repos pr' and no 'gh pr'

pass: The installer gains --github and --azure flags; the chosen provider's command set is merged into the template render context.
fail: Templates keep hard-coded gh pr commands and the installer has no provider flag.

anchors.statement: The lite hook's transition logic must live in one Python file organized by transition type.
anchors.quote: The business logic is to be in a single small python file which is organized by transition type and enums w/ exhaustive checks (that will compile error if not handled)
anchors.summary: Lite hook: one file, organized by transition type
anchors.scope: adds or changes the lite hook atm-bd-task-hook.py or splits logic out of it
anchors.deterministic_check: no module under skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts other than atm-bd-task-hook.py calls bd close, bd update, atm task or git

pass: All dev, fix and qa close transitions are implemented in skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts/atm-bd-task-hook.py, one section per transition.
fail: The lite close logic is split across hook.py, qa_close.py and dispatch.py helper modules.

anchors.statement: Every transition in the lite hook must be an enum matched exhaustively, so that a missing arm fails pyright strict.
anchors.quote: The business logic is to be in a single small python file which is organized by transition type and enums w/ exhaustive checks (that will compile error if not handled)
anchors.scope: adds or changes transition handling in the lite hook
anchors.deterministic_check: pyright --strict on atm-bd-task-hook.py with reportMatchNotExhaustive=error reports 0 errors

pass: Transition is a StrEnum and every handler uses match with no default arm; pyright strict reportMatchNotExhaustive is on.
fail: Transitions are compared as strings in if/elif chains with a final else that logs unknown.

anchors.statement: Lite hook tests must put each repeated setup or assertion pattern in a shared helper method.
anchors.quote: I want less code in the business logic.  test code is fine, but should be written efficiently w/ repeated patterns using common methods.
anchors.summary: Tests share repeated patterns via helpers
anchors.scope: adds or changes tests for the lite hook or lite cron
anchors.deterministic_check: a duplicate-block scan over skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts/tests finds no repeated block longer than 5 lines

pass: Tests build hooks through a make_close_vars() and run_hook() helper shared by every case.
fail: Each test repeats the twelve-line close-vars setup and subprocess stub inline.

anchors.statement: The atm-bd console, cron and queues commands must serve lite and full phases through one unchanged command-line interface.
anchors.quote: Some items would be atm-bd-<profile> specific i.e. atm-bd-task-hook.py the task assignment j2 templates, the cron script.  We should use the same tool interfaces for atm-bd cron, atm-bd console, atm-bd queues (and others I may have missed).  This would mean that there would need to be atm-bd-core types that are shared between all profiles and I expect we would want the same schema, although atm-bd-lite would allow some mandetory schema items to be 'undefined' i.e. sanity.
anchors.summary: Same tool interfaces for both profiles
anchors.scope: adds or changes atm-bd console, cron, queues, sprint-report or bv-analyze
anchors.deterministic_check: atm-bd console/cron/queues --help text is unchanged, and the lite fixture phase renders in each with no profile flag

pass: atm-bd console, cron and queues read profile from the phase toml and render the lite phase with the same arguments as today.
fail: A new atm-bd lite-console command is added for lite phases.

anchors.statement: Both profiles must use the single bead schema defined in atm-bd-core.
anchors.quote: Some items would be atm-bd-<profile> specific i.e. atm-bd-task-hook.py the task assignment j2 templates, the cron script.  We should use the same tool interfaces for atm-bd cron, atm-bd console, atm-bd queues (and others I may have missed).  This would mean that there would need to be atm-bd-core types that are shared between all profiles and I expect we would want the same schema, although atm-bd-lite would allow some mandetory schema items to be 'undefined' i.e. sanity.
anchors.summary: One core schema for both profiles
anchors.scope: adds or changes bead_schema, close_fields, bead models or formulas
anchors.deterministic_check: skills/atm-bd-lite contains no schema or TypedDict model files

pass: Lite beads validate against core bead_schema models; no schema file is added under skills/atm-bd-lite.

anchors.statement: In the lite profile the sanity fields of the shared schema must be optional, left undefined rather than filled.
anchors.quote: Some items would be atm-bd-<profile> specific i.e. atm-bd-task-hook.py the task assignment j2 templates, the cron script.  We should use the same tool interfaces for atm-bd cron, atm-bd console, atm-bd queues (and others I may have missed).  This would mean that there would need to be atm-bd-core types that are shared between all profiles and I expect we would want the same schema, although atm-bd-lite would allow some mandetory schema items to be 'undefined' i.e. sanity.
anchors.summary: Lite leaves sanity schema fields undefined
anchors.scope: adds or changes bead_schema, close_fields or close vars
anchors.deterministic_check: core bead_schema and CloseFields mark sanity_bead and max_sanity_rounds NotRequired, and a lite close-vars fixture without them validates

pass: sanity_bead and max_sanity_rounds are NotRequired in CloseFields and lite close vars omit them.
fail: Lite close vars set sanity_bead to the string none to satisfy the required field.

anchors.statement: Scripts and templates of either profile never invoke the gh stack subcommand or the GitHub stacks API.
anchors.quote: One item that also needs to be addressed both ATM – BD – lite and ATM – BD – orchestration is for GH stacking to work on non-GitHub repos, a.k.a. azure git repos.  This is something we should address at ATM BD lite phase buy only checking the base and top of work trees, not using the GH stack sub command
anchors.scope: adds or changes stack linking, stack checks, sanity-stack-link, or dispatch templates
anchors.deterministic_check: grep -rn 'gh stack\|/stacks' over core/ and skills/ (*.py, *.j2, sanity-stack-link) finds nothing

pass: sanity-stack-link records layers in the stack bead and sets the PR base with the provider command; no gh stack call remains.
fail: The lite hook calls gh stack link to attach the layer.

anchors.statement: Stack checks must compare the PR base with the stack top using git alone.
anchors.quote: One item that also needs to be addressed both ATM – BD – lite and ATM – BD – orchestration is for GH stacking to work on non-GitHub repos, a.k.a. azure git repos.  This is something we should address at ATM BD lite phase buy only checking the base and top of work trees, not using the GH stack sub command
anchors.scope: adds or changes the stack gate or stack linking
anchors.deterministic_check: stack_gate.py subprocess calls are git only; a test with an Azure-style remote URL passes the gate

pass: stack_gate.check runs git merge-base --is-ancestor on origin/<base> and head and compares the base ref to the stack top branch.
fail: The stack check queries the GitHub stacks API for the stack's top PR.

anchors.statement: The dev and fix close hook must refuse the close when the PR base differs from the stack top, before running bd close and atm task close.
anchors.quote: 1) dev/fix 'atm task close' would check pr base vs. stack top (blocking close if not stacked properly) then do bd close, atm task close.
anchors.summary: Close hook: stack gate blocks, then bd close, then task close
anchors.scope: adds or changes a dev or fix close hook or the stack gate
anchors.deterministic_check: a hook test with PR base != stack top exits non-zero with no bd or atm subprocess recorded

pass: On NotStacked the hook exits 2 with the fix command before any bd close or atm task close subprocess.
fail: The hook runs bd close first and then warns that the PR base does not match the stack top.

anchors.statement: A phase never contains beads of more than one profile.
anchors.quote: 2) never mix profiles in the same phase.
anchors.scope: adds or changes phase-config, validate-plan, bead-groups or bead_schema
anchors.deterministic_check: validate-plan on a lite phase containing a stage:dev-sanity bead exits 5

pass: validate-plan exits 5 when a lite phase contains a stage:dev-sanity bead.
fail: A phase mixes lite sprints and full sprints by setting profile per sprint bead.

anchors.statement: Profile-specific scripts and templates must live under their own skill directory, skills/<profile>/scripts and skills/<profile>/templates.
anchors.quote: i would expect the atm-bd-lite only scripts to be in skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts/  and templates in atm-bd-lite/templates/ w/ corresponding atm-bd-orchestration scripts/stemplates located relative to the skill.  scripts/templates would be at a common point (which perhaps would best be at repo root in .atm-bd/scripts and /templates.  That would remove duplicates across .claude/ .codex/ and .agents/ that exist today
anchors.summary: Profile files live under the profile skill
anchors.scope: adds or moves scripts or templates of a profile
anchors.deterministic_check: the full profile's hook, sanity scripts and dev/fix/sanity templates sit under skills/atm-bd-orchestration; the lite hook, cron and templates sit under skills/atm-bd-lite

pass: atm-bd-task-hook.py, lite_cron.py and the lite dev/fix/qa templates sit under skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts and templates.
fail: The lite hook is placed in core/scripts next to the shared modules.

anchors.statement: Shared scripts and templates must be installed once, to .atm-bd/scripts and .atm-bd/templates at the repository root.
anchors.quote: i would expect the atm-bd-lite only scripts to be in skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts/  and templates in atm-bd-lite/templates/ w/ corresponding atm-bd-orchestration scripts/stemplates located relative to the skill.  scripts/templates would be at a common point (which perhaps would best be at repo root in .atm-bd/scripts and /templates.  That would remove duplicates across .claude/ .codex/ and .agents/ that exist today
anchors.scope: adds, moves or installs shared scripts or templates
anchors.deterministic_check: after install, no file under .atm-bd/scripts or .atm-bd/templates also exists under .claude/skills, .codex/skills or .agents

pass: core/scripts and core/templates install to .atm-bd/scripts and .atm-bd/templates; the skill directories no longer carry copies.
fail: Shared modules are copied into .claude/skills and .codex/skills on install as before.

anchors.statement: The atm-bd-lite profile must ship its own task-close hook file, separate from the full profile's atm-task-close.py.
anchors.quote: the atm-bd-lite would have a completely different atm-task-hook python file.
anchors.summary: Lite has its own hook file
anchors.scope: adds or changes a task-close hook, or selects a hook by profile

pass: skills/atm-bd-lite/scripts/atm-bd-task-hook.py is a separate file; atm-task-close.py is unchanged.
fail: atm-task-close.py gains an if profile == lite branch that skips sanity.

anchors.statement: The lite profile must run a phase end to end with a single agent and no sanity stage.
anchors.quote: we haven't designed 'lite' yet. it will be a much simpler orchestration that could be run by a single agent or small team.
anchors.summary: Lite runs with one agent, no sanity
anchors.scope: adds or changes the lite skill, lite formulas or lite templates
anchors.deterministic_check: the lite sprint-group formula pours dev and qa beads only, and the lite SKILL.md names no sanity member

pass: The lite sprint-group formula pours dev and qa beads; one agent dispatches, develops and closes QA in the live run.
fail: The lite formula pours a sanity bead that a second agent must close before QA.
